summary: Learn SPC, control charts, Cp/Cpk, and capability analysis in 5 days. Build practical quality tools and improve process stability.
lede: Statistical process control and process capability analysis help quality and production professionals assess variation, process stability, and ability to meet specifications. The training is for engineers, quality managers, supervisors, and continuous improvement specialists who need to choose and interpret charts and turn signals into quality actions. It covers subgrouping, variable and attribute charts, capability indices, sampling, and reaction planning, with exercises in capability summaries and quality reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to monitor process variation, interpret control charts, and turn statistical evidence into quality actions. Quality Engineers who monitor process stability and control chart signals. Process Engineers who design subgrouping and variation control methods. QA Managers who review capability studies and corrective actions. Production Supervisors who respond to special-cause signals on the floor. Continuous Improvement Specialists who use SPC in problem-solving. Manufacturing Engineers who align chart selection with process behavior. Quality Control Analysts who calculate defect rates and capability indices. Operations Managers who translate SPC evidence into daily decisions. Supplier Quality Engineers who track incoming and supplier process variation. Lean Six Sigma Practitioners who use SPC within improvement projects.
prerequisites: You should bring a calculator or spreadsheet access and be prepared to work with simple process datasets. If your organisation uses Minitab or equivalent statistical software, you can apply the exercises directly, but software is not required for completion.
